Garbo waste can

Karim Rashid’s curvy polypropylene wastebasket for Umbra, one of the best-known blobjects of the late 1990s.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Mia records a plastic waste can dated 1996, 33.2 × 26.7 × 25.1 cm, designed by Karim Rashid and made by Umbra, and says the “curvaceous, handled Garbo trash can is now a design icon, selling over two million units”. Mia 2001.232.

The Philadelphia Museum of Art gives “designed 1995”, polypropylene, translucent. Philadelphia Museum of Art. Nasjonalmuseet in Oslo dates its copy 1996. Nasjonalmuseet OK-2002-0106.

Metropolis (Misha Volf, 19 January 2016) describes an injection-molded polypropylene can released in 1996 in a “high-intensity color palette”, and says Rashid proposed in early meetings that it be translucent, “passing diffused light through its torso”. Metropolis.

Why it belongs

Garbo is the blobject in domestic form: a cheap molded object made sensual through curves and color. It shows that the Y2K shape language reached everyday goods, not only electronics.

The shape and color are well documented, but no image was inspected, so no visual details are listed here.

Borrow

Give functional openings, such as handles, soft rounded cut-outs instead of separate parts.

Let a container flare outward at the top, so the silhouette reads as a curve, not a box.
